text: So, what kind of conference was I at in Rome anyway? Hey everybody, I'm Dan Mlelen. I'm a scholar of the Bible and religion. And lately, my posts have all
been coming from a conference I was participating in in Rome. And it was part of the Enoch
Seminar, which is a scholarly group that was founded 25 years ago and originally
was more directly focused on First Enoch, but slowly broadened to address second temple Judaism on its own terms
as well as as a context for the rise of Christianity. and they have a few meetings throughout the year, but one
that I've attended twice now is called the Nanjeroni meeting, which is usually around June. Last year was in a little village called Gadada, just outside of
Milan. It was in Rome this year. And uh each meeting has a theme. Last year the
theme was God's body. So there will be a volume coming out probably
end of this year, beginning of next year with a paper of mine in it. And this year the theme was Christology. The
title was from Jewish prophet to Jewish God. And we were talking about
uh how we account for that development regarding the conceptualization of Jesus of Nazareth. And so there were about
25ish uh scholars there. We all submitted abstracts. Some of us were invited to
present and we all took turns uh well the first thing we did was circulate our papers. So everybody got sent all the
papers a few weeks beforehand which gives us time to read through them. And then at the actual conference we took 15
minutes to basically summarize the paper. And then every session had two or
three papers. And then the panelists who were summarizing their papers would interact with each other's papers and
then we would open it up to everybody at the conference to discuss for like an hour or so
uh their thoughts on the papers that were given. And so it's a really collaborative meeting and and an opportunity for people to get feedback
on research they're working on to to hone their arguments and to bounce ideas off of other scholars. And then we also really appreciate the collegiality.
Uh everybody's wonderful. We go have lunch and dinner together. We did an
excursion to the catacombs of Priscilla uh as well as to uh Constantine's uh mausoleum.
And yeah, after everybody gets home, they'll have about 6 months to revise their papers and then submit them to

how many people in the room thought that uh any of the texts of the New Testament, any of the authors of the New
